validity.recommendation: Keep the row (real, distinct AGP subsea segment). Reconcile LengthKnown 18 km against the independently and repeatedly sourced 15 km subsea crossing figure; note capacity 10.30 bcm/y is the whole-line AGP design figure shared with P0436 (a segment throughput, not additive).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. This is the subsea Gulf-of-Aqaba crossing of Arab Gas Pipeline Phase 1 (El Arish-Aqaba), inaugurated July 2003 by President Mubarak and King Abdullah II - which is exactly what the sheet's own Arabic ref (kingabdullah.jo, 'gas line between El Arish and Aqaba', ok=200) documents. Offshore-technology, Wikipedia and oilandgasadvancement all independently describe the '15km subsea pipeline from Taba to Aqaba' as a built, commissioned segment. Not phantom. CLASSIFICATION: correct - a gas transmission trunk (cross-border export line, not gathering/process/feeder; Fuel=Gas correct). DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. P0436 (Arab Gas Pipeline, El Arish->'South Sinai', 250 km, 36 in) is the onshore Sinai overland segment El Arish->Taba; P7482 is the 15-18 km / 26 in subsea Taba->Aqaba crossing. They are complementary AGP Phase-1 segments deliberately split (RouteNotes 'IM: updated 2025 to reflect individual segment'), corroborated by sources that give 250 km onshore @36in + 15 km subsea @26in. GulfPub merges the whole Egyptian AGP into ONE feature (169 km, 36 in, El Arish->Aqaba) - i.e. GulfPub is the un-split version, not evidence of a GEM internal dup. Caveat: capacity 10.30 bcm/y is identical on P0436 and P7482 because it is the entire AGP nameplate (offshore-technology & Wikipedia both give 10.3 bcm/y for the line); correct as a per-segment throughput but must NOT be summed across segments. SPEC: Diameter 26 in CONFIRMED (Wikipedia + trade sources agree the subsea crossing is 26 in vs the 36 in onshore trunk). StartYear 2003 CONFIRMED (July 2003 commissioning, multiple independent sources). Capacity 10.3 bcm/y CONFIRMED as line design. LENGTH is the one discrepancy: GEM=18 km, but offshore-technology, oilandgasadvancement and Wikipedia all say 15 km for the Taba-Aqaba subsea segment - a ~20% overstatement; flag, do not silently pass.

validity.researcher_notes: Operator [ref] is blank (MISSING_REF). GEM Operator='Egyptian Natural Gas Co' (GASCO), Owner='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100%. Offshore-technology names the Egyptian consortium that built and operates (30-yr BOOT) the El Arish-Aqaba section as EGAS, ENPPI, Petrojet and GASCO - GASCO being Egypt's gas-transmission operator - which supports the GASCO/EGAS attribution. GulfPub's auto-flag maps AGP to 'East Mediterranean Gas Company (EMG)'; EMG is the El Arish->Ashkelon (Israel) line operator, a GulfPub misattribution for the Aqaba crossing. GEM attribution defensible; single strong source -> medium.

routes.start_name: Taba, South Sinai, Egypt (Egyptian coast at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba)
routes.end_name: Aqaba, Jordan (AGP receiving landfall near the Aqaba industrial/power zone)
routes.corridor_desc: Short subsea gas line crossing the northern head of the Gulf of Aqaba. It leaves the Egyptian coast at/near Taba (Egypt-Israel border) and runs diagonally SE across the gulf head, passing south of the Israeli (Eilat) tripoint waters, to make landfall on the Jordanian coast at Aqaba. Straight-line Taba->Aqaba is ~13-15 km, matching the independently sourced 15 km subsea length (GEM lists 18 km). Corridor is tightly bounded by the narrow gulf head and the two named landfalls; the exact subsea alignment (single crossing vs slight dogleg south of Eilat) is not sourced to meters, so no interior waypoint is asserted.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the sheet + independent sources naming 'Taba to Aqaba' as the subsea crossing. Coordinates are for the real towns/landfalls: Taba (~29.49N, 34.90E) and Aqaba (~29.52N, 35.00E, landfall near the Aqaba power/industrial zone south of the city). No coordinate fabricated; no interior waypoint invented because the precise submarine path is not published.

summary: P7482 Arab Gas Pipeline Taba-Aqaba subsea crossing: real, correctly classified gas transmission, NOT a duplicate of onshore P0436 - confirmed (caveat); concern_types spec (length 18 km vs sourced 15 km; capacity 10.3 bcm/y is whole-line, shared with P0436) + attribution (GASCO/EGAS defensible, GulfPub's EMG is a misattribution; filled missing Operator [ref]).
